answers.ask: Thirty seconds of running works out around 500 studs at walk speed — should the street be about that long, or longer as he speeds up?
answers.answer: Make the street about 500 studs long for the intended roughly 30-second run; keep the pace consistent rather than extending the course for speed boosts.

answers.ask: Once he reaches Andy, does the game end, or does the course loop and get harder?
answers.answer: Reaching Andy ends the run as a win.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D endless-runner-style neighborhood street course about 500 studs long, arranged as a straight three-lane road. Gloo, a light-brown mini goldendoodle, runs down the center of the scene through incoming cars, garbage trucks, pedestrians blocking lanes, ground trash, and low overhead obstacles, with dog treats placed along the road. Neighborhood buildings and sidewalks frame both sides of the street. At the far end of the course, Andy, an Asian man with glasses, waits as the finish-point figure.
agent_notes: Self-declared subway-surfer type with automatic forward running and three fixed lanes, so Infinite Runner on lane-snap; the course terminating at Andy rather than running forever does not contradict the genre, since the player never controls their own speed and never chooses discrete jumps, so it is a lane runner with a finish rather than Racing or Obby. Kept Lane Runner for the shape, moving traffic and ground pickups but dropped chunk-modular, because the answers fix the street at about 500 studs for a single roughly 30-second authored run, so there is no long chunk queue to keep from drifting. Added obstacle-jump for the trash, powerup-buffs for the treats, marker-distance for the distance score, and hazard-kill for the traffic that ultimately ends the run — noting the run survives two trips and only ends on the third, when animal control takes him. Without a user I decided the duck-under obstacles ride along with the hurdle row since no option covers overhead barriers, that Andy is npc-population as the named figure at the end and marks where the run pays off, that the blocking Karens are static lane obstacles rather than ambient population, and that settlement-density carries the suburban street the whole track runs through.
